clue.text: Part of garden in which ruler gets covered in soil

indicators.note: in which says the ruler sits inside the garden part, splitting it open

parts.note: a flower bed is part of a garden
an emir is a Muslim ruler

explanation.surface: A garden plot where a king or sultan is buried in earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets' is a link word joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Mired means stuck in mud, so to be be-mired is to be dirtied with soil or mud.

clue.text: Lose hope of boy finding still water

parts.note: Des is a short form of the boy's name Desmond
a pond holds still, non-flowing water

explanation.surface: Someone despairs of a lad who has discovered a pond.
explanation.definitionFit: To despond is an old verb meaning to lose heart or become dejected.

clue.text: Fool set about making cash

indicators.note: set about read as 'turned around' tells us to write the word for fool backwards

parts.note: nit (short for nitwit) is a fool

explanation.surface: A foolish person sets about making money.
explanation.definitionFit: Tin is old British slang for money.

clue.text: Footballer and comic actor? They do well in bookshops

parts.note: George Best was a famous Northern Irish footballer
Peter Sellers was a British comic actor

explanation.surface: Asks whether a sportsman and a comedian are big sellers in book stores.
explanation.definitionFit: Bestsellers are books that sell in great numbers, so they do well in shops.

clue.text: More than one home or house having substances in jars?

parts.note: spices are kept in jars in the kitchen

explanation.surface: Asks about homes or houses that keep things in jars.
explanation.definitionFit: A hospice is a home for the terminally ill, so the plural covers more than one such home.

clue.text: Bank in south London district not in good shape

indicators.note: not tells us to remove the following phrase's synonym from the district name

parts.note: Camberwell is a district of south London
well means in good health or shape

explanation.surface: A riverbank in a run-down part of south London.
explanation.walkthrough: CAMBERWELL is a district in south London.
explanation.definitionFit: A camber is the sideways slope or banking of a road surface.

clue.text: Minimal power cut? Thank goodness for that!

indicators.note: Minimal asks for the smallest possible part, the first letter of the word that follows

parts.note: to hew is to cut, as with an axe

explanation.surface: Relief at a power cut being only very brief.
explanation.definitionFit: Phew is an exclamation of relief, said when something worrying has passed.

clue.text: Yelling with stick when love affair is admitted

indicators.note: is admitted says the affair is let into the word for stick

parts.note: to cling is to stick fast
an amour is a love affair

explanation.surface: Someone shouting and wielding a stick on learning of an affair.
explanation.definitionFit: Clamouring means making a loud insistent noise, i.e. shouting or yelling.

clue.text: Bearing's components swapped around, sinking

indicators.note: components swapped around says the two parts of the word for bearing change places

parts.note: undergoing means bearing or enduring

explanation.surface: A mechanic swaps the parts of a ball bearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Going under means sinking below the surface, as a ship does.

clue.text: A flawless person recalled as great

indicators.note: recalled, read as called back, tells us to read the phrase backwards

parts.note: a gem is a person of great worth, without flaw

explanation.surface: A perfect person is remembered as great.
explanation.definitionFit: Mega is informal slang for great or excellent.

clue.text: The devilish underworld can alarm

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, and the underworld itself
may means can, as in 'you may go'

explanation.surface: A hellish netherworld can be frightening.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismay is to alarm or fill with consternation.

clue.text: Dog and master spotted in European capital after party

indicators.note: after puts the capital piece behind the party

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: spotted in says the master is seen inside the city name

parts.note: Bern is the capital of Switzerland
MA is Master of Arts

explanation.surface: A dog and its owner seen in a European city after a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A Dobermann is a breed of large guard dog.

clue.text: A lad should lose yen for road race — it's a disgrace

indicators.note: should lose says the letter for yen is dropped from the boy

parts.note: a lad is a boy
Y is the abbreviation for yen, the Japanese currency
MI stands for the M1, Britain's first motorway
a nation is a race of people

explanation.surface: A youngster should give up his longing for road racing, which is shameful.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is a British motorway, written MI in crosswords. 'for' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: An abomination is something loathsome, a thing that is a disgrace.

clue.text: Bad legal document that's cut wife out

indicators.note: cut together with out tells us to remove the wife's letter from the document
out, with cut, marks the letter being taken away

parts.note: a will is a legal document

explanation.surface: A nasty will that disinherits the testator's spouse.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill can mean bad, as in ill will or ill effects.

clue.text: Financial crisis beginning to end — little hesitation to supply one-off payment

indicators.note: beginning to end tells us to move the first letter of the crisis word to its end

parts.note: a slump is an economic crisis
um is a brief hesitation in speech

explanation.surface: From start to finish of a financial crisis, little delay in making a single payment.
explanation.walkthrough: SLUMP with its S sent to the back gives LUMPS. 'to supply' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A lump sum is a single payment made all at once rather than in instalments.

clue.text: Plants? Insect beginning to starve nibbles first of them

indicators.note: nibbles, as an insect bites into something, puts one letter inside the other piece

parts.note: a louse is an insect

indicators.note: first of asks for the first letter of the following word
beginning to asks for the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Asks whether plants are being nibbled by a starving insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Lotuses are water plants, such as the water lily.

clue.text: Bungling bishop lost touch with head of parish

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

indicators.note: lost suggests confusion, so the letters of the word touch are rearranged
head of asks for the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A clumsy bishop has lost contact with his parish priest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' turns TOUCH into OTCHU. 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A botch-up is a bungled job; bungling as a noun is the same act of messing something up.

clue.text: Given external funds, plant religious institutions

indicators.note: Given external says the funds word is put around the plant

parts.note: monies means funds
an aster is a flowering plant

explanation.surface: Religious houses plant flowers when given outside money.
explanation.definitionFit: Monasteries are religious houses where monks live.

clue.text: Teachers seen as poor performers, wasting time

indicators.note: wasting, as in losing, says the time letter is removed

parts.note: rabbit is British slang for a poor player, especially a weak batsman in cricket

explanation.surface: Teachers judged weak performers for wasting time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen as' is a link. In British sport a rabbit is a hopeless player.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabbi is a Jewish scholar and religious teacher.

clue.text: Getting rid of little woman with a series of letters

parts.note: Di is a short form of the woman's name Diana
spelling sets out the letters of a word in series

explanation.surface: Disposing of a small woman's string of written letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Dispelling means driving away or dismissing, i.e. getting rid of something.

clue.text: Mechanise with 27 leaving part of newspaper office

indicators.note: leaving says the answer to clue 27 is taken out

parts.note: to deskill a job is to mechanise it so it needs no skill
this refers to the answer at 27 across, a word for bad

explanation.surface: A newspaper office is mechanised once someone departs.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper's news desk or sports desk is a department of its office.

clue.text: Short programme on British dish

indicators.note: on in a down clue means the British letter goes after
Short says the programme word loses its last letter

parts.note: a syllabus is a programme of study

explanation.surface: A brief British TV programme about cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: Syllabub is a traditional English dessert of whipped cream and wine.

clue.text: I took the prize for recitation

indicators.note: for recitation means the word is spoken aloud so we hear its sound

parts.note: won means took the prize

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of winning a poetry-reciting contest.
explanation.definitionFit: I is the Roman numeral for one.

clue.text: Cleaning item quiet academician found in archaeological exercise

indicators.note: found in says the pieces are discovered inside the dig

parts.note: a dig is an archaeological excavation
sh is a call for quiet
RA is a Royal Academician

explanation.surface: A cleaning cloth found by a quiet scholar on an excavation.
explanation.definitionFit: A dishrag is a cloth for washing up dishes.

clue.text: Dressed-up females naughty boss admired, nothing becoming one

indicators.note: naughty suggests misbehaving letters, so they are rearranged
becoming says one letter turns into another

parts.note: taken as written before one letter changes
O is the round figure for nothing
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Women dressed up because their wicked boss liked nothing better.
explanation.walkthrough: In BOSSADMIRED the O becomes I, and the letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Bridesmaids are the women attending a bride, all dressed up for the wedding.

clue.text: Ancient note penned by this writer's heartless opponent

parts.note: this writer's is I'm, i.e. I am
a memo is a short note

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter is removed

parts.note: a rival is an opponent

explanation.surface: A writer's adversary has heartlessly sent an ancient note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penned by' is a link, picturing the note written by this writer: I'M then MEMO. 'heartless' takes the middle V out of RIVAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Immemorial means extending back beyond memory, so very old or ancient.

clue.text: Saint rarely using it to pen article

indicators.note: rarely, read as unusually, says the letters are arranged in an uncommon way

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A saint who seldom uses it to write a piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to pen' is a link: the letters of USING, IT and A are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Ignatius of Loyola founded the Jesuits.

clue.text: Duck with grand bill on top of barrier

indicators.note: on top of in a down clue puts the first pieces above the barrier

parts.note: G is short for grand, a thousand
an ad is a bill or advertisement
a wall is a barrier

explanation.surface: A duck with an impressive beak perched on a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: The gadwall is a species of dabbling duck.

clue.text: Ring to declare invalid not fit for operation

parts.note: to annul is to declare invalid
US is short for unserviceable, unfit for use

explanation.surface: A ring is declared void and unusable.
explanation.definitionFit: An annulus is a ring-shaped figure.

clue.text: For food plant, foreign character put in soil modifier

indicators.note: put in says the Greek letter goes inside

parts.note: peat is added to soil to improve it
nu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek gardener puts a soil improver in for a food crop.
explanation.definitionFit: The peanut, or groundnut, is a plant grown for food.

clue.text: Element of herbal medicine maybe

indicators.note: Element of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Something that might be part of a herbal remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition 'maybe' cannot stand for the answer; the whole clue is the definition, since balm is a herb used in remedies.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemon balm is a herb used in herbal remedies, so it may well be an ingredient of one.

clue.text: Report of Cockney in resistance unit

indicators.note: Report of says the word is heard spoken

parts.note: in means at home, and a Cockney drops the h, saying 'ome

explanation.surface: A news report from a London dweller about electrical resistance.
explanation.definitionFit: The ohm is the SI unit of electrical resistance.
